newsitem.title: LATVIA: RIGA CITY BUYS MERCEDES' BUSES.
newsitem.headline: RIGA CITY BUYS MERCEDES' BUSES.

text.p: Riga city council said on Friday that it has signed an agreement with Mercedes-Benz to buy 52 buses worth 11.43 million marks, financed by a World Bank infrastructure loan.
"The agreement will give the capital 52 buses of which six will be articulated," Andris Grinbergs, city managing director, told Reuters.
"The first deliveries from the company's plant in Turkey are due in 18 weeks and we hope to have the buses running by Latvian Independence Day on November 18," Grinbergs said.
Mercedes won a tender contested by six companies including Swedish Volvo, Scania and Hungarian Ikarus.
Ikarus during the 1970s and 1980s delivered most of Riga's current 320-strong bus fleet.
The World Bank loan is for 17 years and worth $16.8 million. It has an average interest rate of seven percent.
The loan will also fund the purchase of 42 trolley-buses in a tender won by Czech Skoda.
"The total sum of this trolley-bus purchase is being finalised at the moment," Grinbergs said.
